LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING - SMS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when writing an SMS, • use SMS observing etiquette. How do we ensure etiquette when using digital devices?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information
2. create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 1.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING - SMS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 1.3.1 SOCIAL WRITING - SMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS to a partner. (skill: create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information.
3. Practise this skill: create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when writing an SMS, • use SMS observing etiquette. How do we ensure etiquette when using digital devices?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 1.3.1 Social writing - SMS means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify features of a Short Message Service (SMS) for information.
5. Be able to: create an SMS text with appropriate features for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
